Collection or Subsection Name: UK retail industry: changes on the high street

Oddbins is an off-licence retail chain in the United Kingdom, established in 1963. On 1 February 2019, Oddbins again went into administration.
Edinburgh Woollen Mill is a retailer specialising in clothing.

Mackays Stores Limited, trading under the name M&Co., is a Scottish chain store selling clothes and small homewear products. The company was established in 1834 and is currently based in Renfrewshire, Scotland.

Topshop is a British multinational fashion retailer of clothing, shoes, make-up and accessories. It has around 500 shops worldwide – of which some 300 are in the UK – plus online operations in a number of its markets.

Arcadia Group Ltd. is a British multinational retailing company headquartered in London, United Kingdom. It owns the high street clothing retailers Burton, Dorothy Perkins, Evans, Miss Selfridge, Topman, Topshop, Wallis and the out of town chain Outfit, which sells lines from the other group chains.

Laura Ashley plc is a British textile design company
Peacocks is a fast-fashion retail chain based in Cardiff and now part of the Edinburgh Woollen Mill group.

Burton is a British high street menswear clothing retailer which became a trading name of Arcadia Group Brands Ltd, part of the Arcadia Group. The company was founded by Sir Montague Maurice Burton in Chesterfield in 1903 under the name of The Cross-Tailoring Company. It was first listed on the London Stock Exchange in 1929 by which time it had 400 stores, factories and mills.

Wallis is a British women's clothing retailer, a subsidiary of the Arcadia Group. The first store was opened by the founder, Raphael Nat Wallis, in Chapel Market, Islington in 1923. Known from the start for its coats and by the 1940s, the chain had 25 shops and a turnover of 300,000 a year.

Topman is a British multinational men's fashion retailer. Along with its women's clothing counterpart Topshop, Topman is a subsidiary of the Arcadia Group, which also owns Burton, Miss Selfridge, Wallis, Evans and Dorothy Perkins. Topman was created in the UK towards the end of the 1970s to provide a new approach to menswear retailing. Since its creation, Topman has also built an international presence, as it continues to expand throughout the US, Europe, and Asia.

Dorothy Perkins is a multinational women's fashion retailer based in the United Kingdom. Founded in 1909 under the name H. P. Newman, the company changed its trading name to Dorothy Perkins in 1919.In the 1960s, Dorothy Perkins was controlled by the Farmer family, who used to own Winster Hosiery. The Burton Group, later known as Arcadia, purchased Dorothy Perkins in 1979.
Miss Selfridge is a nationwide UK high street store which began as the young fashion section of Selfridges department store in London in 1966. It was acquired by Arcadia Group in July 1999.

Bonmarché is a budget clothing retailer based in Wakefield, West Yorkshire. The business was founded in 1982, and was acquired by the Peacock Group in July 2002. In January 2012, the business was sold for an undisclosed sum to private equity group Sun European Partners. The company was placed into administration on 18 October 2019.

Oliver Sweeney Ltd. manufactures and sells footwear for men in the United Kingdom. Its products also include jackets, gloves, luggage, wallets, belts, socks, and shoe care products. In addition, the company offers shoe repair services. Oliver Sweeney Ltd. was founded in 1990 and is based in Newton Abbot, the United Kingdom. Oliver Sweeney Group was placed in administration in mid-July 2020. The company’s seven stores, which include branches in London's Mayfair, Leadenhall Market and Covent Garden, as well as outlets in Leeds and Manchester, will remain permanently closed.

The Norville Group is an independent family owned business, based in Gloucester in the South-West of England. It went into administration in July 2020 but Bath-based designer eyewear firm Inspecs bought up the manufacturing arm of the business from administrators BDO. Norville's operations were undertaken mainly at the company’s headquarters in Gloucester, with smaller bases in Bolton, Seaham and Livingston.

Jaeger is an English fashion brand and retailer of menswear and womenswear. Formerly owned by the retail entrepreneur Harold Tilman, it was acquired by the private equity firm Better Capital in 2011. On 10 April 2017, it was announced that the company had entered Administration.

Based in Sheffield, northern England, Go Outdoors was founded in 1998 by Paul Caplan and John Graham and backed by YFM Equity Partners and, latterly, 3i Group III.L. JD Sports bought back its Go Outdoors business for £56.5million after pushing it into administration in June 2020. The retail group hired administrators from corporate finance firm Deloitte after it saw sales hammered by the coronavirus crisis.

Monsoon Accessorize is a British private limited company. It operates two international retail clothing chains – Monsoon and Accessorize. Monsoon Accessorize was started in London in 1973 by Peter Simon, a market-stall trader, and opened its first shop in Beauchamp Place in May of that year. The first Accessorize shop opened in 1984, next door to Monsoon in Covent Garden. On 10 June 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, Monsoon Accessorize went into administration.

Warehouse is a British clothing retail chain, founded in 1976 Warehouse was owned by Aurora Fashions, as were women's fashion brands Coast and Oasis. On 16 April 2020, it was announced that both Warehouse and Oasis had fallen into administration.

The Oasis stores started in 1991. In April 1998 Oasis purchased the Coast stores. In September 2001 the management team of Oasis Stores Plc, acquired the company via Sierra Acquisitions Ltd., supported by PPM Ventures. Sierra Acquisitions Ltd. later became a part of Sierra Holdings Ltd. On 16 April 2020, it was announced that both Oasis and Warehouse had fallen into administration.

Cath Kidston opened her first shop in London's Holland Park in 1993, selling hand-embroidered tea-towels and brightly renovated furniture. It later became known for using vintage fabric and for its iconic print designs. Cath Kidston was undergoing a turnaround plan before the virus was even discovered. The retailer fell into administration earlier in 2020.

Coast is an online British women's clothing retail chain, founded in 1996. Coast is owned by Aurora Fashions, as are women's fashion brands Warehouse and Oasis. On 11 October 2018, Coast entered administration. Karen Millen, another British retailer, bought parts of the Coast brand, such as the website and concessions in department stores (including the transfer of 600 jobs to Karen Millen). Coast is now an online only retail business, with all retail shops and concession stands having been closed.

Mamas & Papas is a UK-based nursery brand and manufacturer supplying prams, pushcjairs, baby products, furniture and maternity wear. It was established in Huddersfield in 1981 by David and Luisa Scacchetti, both of Italian ancestry, whose initial aim was to bring Italian design to the UK baby buggy market. They started the business with a range of coloured corduroy prams imported from Italy. They sold through one local shop of their own and through supplying other stores, until deciding to become a retail brand in 1998. Mamas & Papas were placed into administration on Friday 8 November 2019 and was immediately bought back by other firms controlled by Bluegem Capital, its private equity owner.

L.K.Bennett is a luxury fashion brand, based in London, United Kingdom. The company sells ready-to-wear collections incorporating clothing, shoes, handbags and accessories. The company went into administration on 7 March 2019.

Website of a popular UK retailer.

The former flagship store, Beales in Bournemouth, was established as The Fancy Fair by John Elmes Beale in 1881 and is the biggest department store in Dorset. The chain expanded through acquiring other department stores and continued to run two stores branded as Palmers in Great Yarmouth and Lowestoft until its closure. Beales entered administration on 20 January 2020 and finally closed their remaining stores on 18 March 2020.

Bensons for Beds is the UK’s leading bed retailer, offering a diverse range of beds frames, divans, mattresses and bedroom furniture. Founded in 1950, Bensons for Beds opened the first dedicated bed centre in 1972. The company is based in Accrington, Lancashire. In November 2019, Bensons for Beds was acquired from Steinhoff International by UK- based private equity group Alteri Investors, alongside Harveys and upholstery and bedding manufacturer Relyon. On 30 June 2020, Bensons for Beds went into administration, but Alteri immediately bought it back.

Harveys Furniture was a British retail chain, specialising in living room and dining room furniture, and was once the largest furniture specialist in the United Kingdom, with over 150 stores. Harveys Furniture was established in the United Kingdom in 1966, with its first store opening in Mare Street, East London. It began as a private company, selling textiles and home furnishings. In 2003, Harveys made the decision to move to a furniture only business, removing all textiles from their product portfolio. The company was acquired by Steinhoff International in October 2005. In November 2019, Harveys and Bensons for Beds were acquired by private equity owner, Alteri Investors. On 30 June 2020 Harveys announced the company had officially gone into administration.

Angora Retail (trading as Lombok) entered administration on 26th March 2020. The company, which was founded in 1998 and best known for its dark teak furniture made from reclaimed wood, had previously been through two pre-pack administrations – in 2009, when Privet Capital bought the group, and in 2011, when it was bought by Lombok’s private owner.
